title: Fine-tuning Large Language Model for Automated Algorithm Design

mechanism.domainTask: Preference-based fine-tuning of LLMs for automated algorithm design
mechanism.populationDetail: This paper does not introduce or specify a maintained evolutionary population; EoH/FunSearch are external data-generation and evaluation frameworks.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No elite archive is introduced; the algorithm database is a source of offline training examples from prior search.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Do not transfer population or replacement behavior from the external EoH/FunSearch frameworks to this fine-tuning method.
mechanism.generationDetail: The standalone prompt conditions on the task and function/code skeleton without embedding a selected candidate parent; downstream EoH/FunSearch integration may add their own parent mechanisms.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Scalar fitness ranks the source algorithm database; the paper does not introduce a new evaluator feedback channel for subsequent generations.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Ranked positive and negative algorithms are training examples; they are not evolutionary parents selected for offspring generation.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The main intervention is offline DPO model-weight adaptation using a diversity-aware rank-bucket preference-pair sampler rather than a new evolutionary search operator.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/FINE-TUNING LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL FOR AUTOMATED ALGORITHM DESIGN.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Currently cited only in Survey/sections/conclusion.tex for adapting models from search-generated databases. The PDF is arXiv:2507.10614v1 (2025), but Survey/reference.bib records year 2026. Treat Llama 1B/8B as separate single-model runs, not a jointly used multi-model system. Explore/exploit balance concerns offline training-pair sampling, not the downstream search controller.
